name: ロサンゼルス（organic&natural Los Angeles） (Los Angeles (Organic & Natural Los Angeles))

claims.text: Savory items include teriyaki and ginger 'steak' preparations made with soy-based mock meat; these typically involve wheat-containing soy sauce/seasonings, so celiac diners should confirm each dish rather than assume it is gluten-free.
Fully vegan kitchen with no meat, eggs, dairy, or animal fats, and homemade animal-free dressings - very low risk of accidental animal ingredients.
Daily handmade gluten-free vegan muffins are made with rice flour, and gluten-free sweets are a regular offering.
Vegetables come from named pesticide-free local farms (Tomofarm, Eco Farm Okuno) and include Kaga vegetables, with pesticide-free Isehikari rice.

name: LOVE for ALL（ラブ フォー オール） (Love for All)

claims.text: The restaurant accommodates a wide range of dietary needs including gluten-free, vegan, vegetarian, soy-free, onion-free, and garlic-free, and all dishes are handmade from scratch with carefully selected ingredients.
Tabelog's listing states all menu items are gluten-free.
The menu is plant-based and animal-product-free, with the signature lotus-root burger offering a gluten-free bun and vegan cheese.
Cooking avoids chemical preservatives, artificial colors, chemical seasonings, and refined sugar, with explicit soy-free, onion-free, and garlic-free options.

米粉シフォン専門店 — the shop works only with rice flour and gluten-free ingredients, but no dedicated/certified GF-kitchen claim was found; oatmeal used in some bakes can carry wheat cross-contact unless certified.
Not applicable — dessert/bakery shop, no soy-sauce dishes.
Egg-containing chiffon batter and egg-free cookies are made in the same shop; ask if strictly vegan.
Owner reportedly created the recipes for a child's allergies, indicating strong allergy awareness.
Entire lineup is rice-flour based; several bakes are 「小麦粉や乳製品、卵不使用」.

name: Natural Grocery Store midoriya（ミドリヤ） (Natural Grocery Store midoriya)

claims.text: Baked goods are made fresh in an open kitchen; most are rice-flour gluten-free, but scones are not gluten-free, so wheat is present in the same kitchen. No celiac-grade cross-contamination protocol is documented.
All house-made baked goods and drinks are stated to contain no animal-derived ingredients (no eggs, butter or dairy), so vegan cross-contact risk in the cafe items is low.

The owner curates products with a focus on items children can safely enjoy and labels baked goods as egg/butter/wheat-free where applicable, but no formal allergy protocol is documented; ask about specific items in person.
Sweets are made with rice flour and are vegan, with gluten-free options clearly the focus of the menu.
Egg-free and dairy-free options are available, with explicit vegan and gluten-free framing throughout the menu.

name: Petit pas (お米の粉の研究所 プティパ)

claims.text: No wheat flour is used anywhere in the shop - all bread is 100% rice flour and all cakes are wheat-flour-free, so ambient flour cross-contact is essentially eliminated.
Dairy and eggs are used in cakes and some sandwiches; shared prep with vegan items not documented.
Owners are wheat-allergic themselves and built the shop around gluten-free baking; phone 076-298-1181 to confirm specifics.
「当店のケーキ・デザートはすべて小麦粉不使用です」- all cakes and desserts are wheat-flour-free; 「すべて国産米粉パン」- all bread is domestic rice flour.

name: Hakusan Quiche House QUI (白山キッシュハウス QUI)

claims.text: 「当店のキッシュは全てグルテンフリーとなっております。」 — all quiches are gluten-free; crust ingredient list shows rice flour (米粉/白山市製造), corn starch, almond powder, rice oil — no wheat listed.
claims.source: https://www.qui-hakusan.com/products/おすすめの米粉キッシュセット

claims.text: 「全ての商品が同じ場所で作られておりますので、アレルギーをお持ちの方はご注意ください」 — a shared-facility caveat, but it is written for egg/dairy; NO explicit wheat/gluten cross-contamination statement or dedicated-kitchen guarantee is published. Confirm wheat handling by phone.
claims.source: https://www.qui-hakusan.com/products/おすすめの米粉キッシュセット

claims.text: 「小麦アレルギーの方でも安心して食べられるように、グルテンフリーになっています」 — tourism corroboration that the shop is gluten-free so wheat-allergic guests can eat safely.

No soy-sauce/tamari statement is published. The shop labels allergens per item (e.g. a pizza page lists shrimp and dairy), showing allergen disclosure, but savory-seasoning (醤油) wheat content is not documented — ask if ordering savory items.
Standard menu is not vegan (all quiches contain egg, most contain cheese); vegan items appear only as rotating specials, so everyday vegan cross-contact handling is not documented.
The shop discloses per-item allergens (egg, dairy, shrimp, etc.) but publishes no documented staff gluten-handling protocol beyond the whole-menu gluten-free branding.
claims.source: https://www.qui-hakusan.com/products/おすすめの米粉キッシュセット

claims.text: Entire menu is 100% rice-flour and branded gluten-free; the crust uses rice flour milled in Hakusan with no wheat, and no wheat products are made on-site.
Certified Hakusan City local-production-consumption recommended shop; discloses allergens per item.

name: SHIROM Creperie (シロームクレープリー)

claims.text: No source addresses shared vs. dedicated griddle, separate prep or flour-dust handling — cross-contact status is unpublished and unknown.
A celiac/GF blogger (米粉とひのことひつじ) reported eating there with essentially no reaction — encouraging but a single anecdote, not a protocol.
Galettes are savory (Noto pork ragù, egg/cheese); no source specifies soy sauce or tamari use. Assume standard wheat-based seasonings unless confirmed.
Not vegan; butter, cream, cheese and egg are used throughout, so plant-based cross-contact is unmanaged.
No published allergy-handling policy; owner directs customers to Instagram DM for reservations and questions.
Dessert crepes are documented as 100% Ishikawa rice flour, 小麦粉不使用 (no wheat flour) gluten-free.
Press states the shop aims to make all products gluten-free-compatible: 「全てグルテンフリーに対応した商品にする」.

Wheat-based pita bread is central to the falafel sandwich and is served alongside hummus, so wheat is handled in the kitchen and the menu is not celiac-safe despite some rice-flour sweets being available.
The cafe is fully plant-based, so there is no animal-product cross-contact risk across the menu.
The owner states a mission to provide 'the safest possible meals in Ishikawa,' indicating attention to ingredient safety, though no specific allergen or cross-contamination protocol is documented.
Entirely vegan menu, so all dishes are free of meat, fish, dairy and egg.
Offers genuinely gluten-free rice-flour (米粉) sweets — a gateau chocolate made with rice rather than wheat flour — for diners avoiding gluten.
Uses oat milk for coffee and house-made ginger syrup, supporting dairy-free ordering.
